construct=AaEnc shell; variant_status=wild_type; assembly_symmetry=icosahedral; T_number=1; T_number_basis=directly_reported; shell_subunit_count=60; shell_diameter_nm=24; curated_notes=Canonical WT cargo-free T=1 AaEnc assembly. Jones et al. 2023 directly reported a ~24 nm icosahedral cage composed of 
60 AaEnc protomers. At pH 7.5, cryo-EM resolved closed (8DN9 / EMD-27558; ~68%) and open (8DNL / EMD-27573; ~32%) five-fold pore states, while at pH 3.0 only the closed state was observed (8DNA / EMD-27560). These structures retain the same global T=1 architecture and are therefore treated as pore conformations of a single assembly rather than separate assemblies. Individual shells remained ~24 nm by TEM across the tested pH range; larger DLS diameters at acidic pH were attributed to limited aggregation, not shell expansion. Reported thermal values are aggregation temperatures (T_agg), not melting temperatures, so thermostability_tm_c is left blank. Heterologous eGFP-TP loading did not produce a distinct shell architecture.
method:
cryo-EM; negative-stain TEM; 
DLS; SEC; static light scattering
condition:
recombinant cargo-free WT AaEnc expressed in 
E. coli BL21(DE3); purified assembled shell; cryo-EM at pH 7.5 (closed and open five-fold pore classes) and pH 3.0 (closed five-fold pore state); biophysical pH-stability characterization across acidic to neutral conditions
